preamble: Final-obstruent devoicing is a phonetic process where voiced fricatives, such as the labiodental [v], lose their voicing at the end of a word or syllable. This shift is a characteristic feature of several language families, including Germanic and Slavic.

examples.note: Word-final devoicing of [v] to [f] in German.
Final [v] in loanwords is regularly devoiced.
Dutch final devoicing: 'ik leef' (I live) is pronounced with [f].
Devoicing after the uvular; cf. Inuktitut arvik
Devoicing before t; Erzya keeps v (кавто)
